requirement:
In authored book chapters, a passage opted into citation review under
{cite}`requirements.references.citation_review.book_commentary` displays its
body as ordinary Markdown prose, with the same left alignment as the
surrounding prose and no opening citation badge or enclosing border.

A small marker in the right gutter identifies the passage's citation-checking
annotations. It does not claim that recorded evidence is current or accepted.
The outermost eligible citation fence has one marker; nested commentary
belongs to its list rather than displaying another marker.

Activating the marker opens the list of resolved citations from the source
passage, including its opening citation, citation-only metadata paragraphs,
and citations within nested commentary. Citations belonging to nested
requirement or example declarations are excluded. Repeated citations appear
once. Project citations link to their declarations; built-in citations retain
their descriptive hover text. The marker is keyboard operable, has an
accessible label, and shows visible keyboard focus. Opening the list does not
hide the passage. Inline citations within explanatory prose retain their
usual rendering.

Rendering does not change the source passage, its discovered references, or
its review inputs. Unfenced citations, citations inside requirement or example
declarations, and utility-only commentary retain their existing rendering.
rationale:
Both reviewed tests carry `{test}` references to the subject. Together they cover each obligation in `requirements.references.citation_review.book_commentary.display`. I did not request implementation source. **Main test: `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[reviewed_passages_show_one_gutter_list_and_preserve_prose_and_literal_contexts]`** - **Prose display, no opening badge or border.** - Parsing the output with pulldown_cmark gives `

The ordinary paragraph cites…

`, `

Nested prose.

` and `

Utility-only.

`. - The prose after `` has no `alt="cite rules.other"` badge from the metadata paragraph. - It has exactly one `cite rules.ready` badge, the explicit inline one. This shows that neither the opening badge nor the nested fence's badge is rendered in the prose. - The nested `::::{cite} rules.ready` fence text is removed from the prose. - **Left alignment and no border.** The CSS `.habeas-citation-passage` rule is checked for `padding: 0;`, `border: 0;` and a left margin of `0`. The margin check parses the shorthand forms. - **One right-gutter marker.** - The output has exactly one `habeas-citation-passage` and one `habeas-citation-list`, even though the passage contains nested commentary. - The CSS for `.habeas-citation-list` is `position: absolute` with `right:` and no `left:`. - The passage is `position: relative`. - The panel CSS has `max-width` and `position: absolute`. - **List contents.** - The list has exactly 4 `
  • ` entries: `habeas:util`, `rules.other`, `rules.ready` and `rules.term_rule`. Each appears once. - This covers the opening citation, the metadata paragraph, nested commentary and the nested definition. - `rules.ready` is cited several times but listed once. - `rules.inside`, which is cited only in the nested req and example, is excluded from the list. - The list has the project link `href="rules.html#habeas-req-rules.other"` and a built-in entry with `habeas-builtin" title=`. - **Accessibility.** - The marker is a native `` with `aria-label="Show citations for this passage"`, a title, and an aria-hidden glyph. - The CSS `:focus-visible` rule is checked for `outline: 2px solid var(--links);`. - **Opening the list does not hide the passage.** The test asserts the sibling structure `\n

    The ordinary paragraph`. Prose is outside the disclosure. - **Existing rendering retained.** - The unfenced outside citation keeps its badge and link, and it is not in the list. - The utility-only fence keeps its fenced-ref rendering and builtin badge. - Nested req and example fences keep their aria-label and link, and their detail chapters carry the `rules.inside` citation. - The test checks that these stay literal: the code-fence, unresolved, HTML-literal and unclosed fences. - **Source unchanged.** The guide file contents and `text_references` are asserted identical before and after rendering. **Supporting test: `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[citation_metadata_is_hidden_in_fenced_sections_and_preserved_in_details]`** - It covers the opening and metadata citations of a `{cite}` fence across the container kinds, including the `{cite}` opening itself. - The `{cite}` opening badge appears exactly once (in the list annotations), and the other citations are hidden from the visible prose. - It also asserts that source files and discovered references are unchanged. I found no obligation without a test and no assertion that contradicts the text. The clause excluding nested requirement or example declarations from the list is tested. The test also expects a nested `definition` citation (`rules.term_rule`) to appear in the list. The text excludes only requirement and example declarations, so that expectation agrees with it.

::::{req} citation_review.book_commentary
A closed `:::{cite} full.name` fence in the book, outside a requirement or
example declaration, opts its explanatory passage into citation review.
A passage needs a review when it contains at least one resolved citation
other than `habeas:util`.
The outermost eligible citation fence identifies the passage. Its opening
citation and citations throughout its body belong to one review, including
citations inside nested commentary containers. References inside nested
requirement or example declarations belong to those declarations' assessments.
The review's subject is the enclosing citation fence's outline node, rather
than the whole chapter. Its inputs include the passage and each cited
declaration or built-in text, with the terminology they use. For project
requirements and examples, the reviewer checks that the passage's claims agree
with and are supported by the cited declarations. Contradicting or unsupported
claims produce a negative assessment. Built-in citations retain their
permitted-role and stated-criteria checks under
{cite}`requirements.references.citation_review`.
These passages use the citation-review storage, freshness checks, selection,
and `author --all` workflow of {cite}`requirements.references.citation_review`.
Their identities follow the existing outline-selector rules. Rendering follows
{cite}`requirements.references.book_badges`. Unfenced book citations retain
their existing behavior.
